prompt:
You are an associate analyst at Marshfield Croft Partners. Andre Thibault, the managing director, has asked you to build a full DCF valuation model for Walt Disney Co. (DIS) as a potential M&A target. The analysis is anchored to the most recent 10-Q filing from May 6, 2026, which covers the quarter ending March 28, 2026, and the team needs a polished, defensible model to support preliminary client discussions.

Build this as a fully dynamic Excel workbook with clearly labeled tabs: Assumptions, Projections (or Income Statement), DCF, Valuation, and Sensitivity. All SEC-sourced base data should be hard-coded on a dedicated inputs section — do not embed raw numbers directly into calculation cells. Format hard-coded inputs in blue font, formulas in black, and cross-tab links in green. The model needs to be audit-friendly: no circular references, no merged cells, and every assumption clearly disclosed.

The base-case inputs must come exclusively from the pinned 10-Q figures: TTM revenues of $51,149M, operating income of $9,203M, net income of $4,649M, total assets of $205,217M, stockholders' equity of $108,708M, cash and cash equivalents of $5,682M, diluted EPS of $2.61, and SG&A expense of $8,194M. These are the only hard-coded starting points — no invented figures.

Build a 5-year unlevered free cash flow projection using the indirect method: start from EBIT, adjust for taxes, add back D&A, subtract CapEx, and subtract changes in net working capital to arrive at UFCF. All projection drivers — revenue growth rate, EBIT margin, D&A as a percentage of revenue, CapEx as a percentage of revenue, NWC assumptions, and effective tax rate — should be adjustable input cells on the Assumptions tab so Andre can toggle scenarios easily. The projection schedule must flow top-down from revenue through EBIT, NOPAT, UFCF, and present value of UFCF.

For terminal value, build in a toggle that lets the user switch between a perpetuity growth method (base-case range of 2.0% to 3.0%) and an exit multiple method (EV/EBITDA range of 10x to 14x) using a single input cell. The WACC calculation should draw from the balance sheet capital structure (equity and debt), a risk-free rate sourced from the 10-year Treasury, an equity risk premium between 5.5% and 6.0%, and a beta pulled from a public comparable set. Include a Comps tab as a placeholder for comparable company multiples — it can be populated later but should be structured now.

From enterprise value, build an equity value bridge that nets out total debt, adds cash, and accounts for minority interests using the balance sheet data. Then roll to an implied equity value per share using diluted shares outstanding (backed into from net income and the $2.61 diluted EPS).

The Sensitivity tab should present a matrix with WACC on the rows and terminal growth rate (or exit multiple, depending on the toggle) on the columns, showing implied equity value per share in each cell. Make this clean enough to paste directly into a deck. Also include a Sources & Uses placeholder tab with clearly marked input cells — it's not active yet but will be needed if this moves to a deal scenario.

Keep all tabs logically organized and ensure a non-technical user can follow the model's flow without needing to trace through every formula. File size should stay reasonable — no external links.

explicit_requirements: Build a fully dynamic 5-year unlevered free cash flow projection starting from the trailing twelve-month revenue and operating income figures.
Calculate a terminal value using both a perpetuity growth method (range: 2.0%-3.0%) and an exit multiple method (EV/EBITDA range: 10x-14x).

Derive the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) using a capital structure based on the latest balance sheet data for debt and equity, a risk-free rate from the 10-year Treasury, an equity risk premium of 5.5%-6.0%, and a beta sourced from a public comparable set.
Produce an enterprise value to equity value bridge that accounts for cash, total debt, and minority interests using the balance sheet data provided.
Sensitivity table showing implied equity value per share across a matrix of WACC (rows) and terminal growth rate or exit multiple (columns).
The model must reference only the pinned SEC facts for base-case inputs; no invented figures.
All tabs in the workbook must be clearly labeled and organized: Assumptions, Projections, Valuation, Sensitivity.
Projections must include revenue growth, EBIT margin, D&A, CapEx, changes in net working capital, and tax rate assumptions, all as adjustable inputs.
The model must be structured so that a non-technical user (e.g., Andre) can toggle between perpetuity growth and exit multiple terminal value methods using a single input cell.
Include a Sources & Uses tab if the model is later adapted for a deal scenario; for now it can be a placeholder with clearly marked inputs.
implicit_requirements: Use the indirect method for deriving UFCF (start with EBIT, adjust for taxes, D&A, CapEx, and changes in NWC).
Hard-code all SEC-sourced base data on a dedicated inputs or data tab; do not embed them directly into calculation cells.
Apply consistent formatting: blue font for hard-coded inputs, black for formulas, green for links to other tabs.
The DCF schedule must flow top-down (revenue → EBIT → NOPAT → UFCF → PV of UFCF → TV → EV → Equity Value → Per Share).
Comparable company multiples for beta and exit multiple should be referenced from a separate Comps tab, even if populated later.
The model must be audit-friendly: no circular references, no merged cells, and all assumptions clearly disclosed.

reference_answer.narrative_prompt:
You are an associate analyst at an investment bank. You have built a 5-year unlevered DCF model for WALT DISNEY CO/ (DIS) based on its latest SEC filings.

The model includes:
- Base-year financials from EDGAR XBRL
- Revenue growth assumption of 4.7% (sector-typical for media)
- WACC of 10.46% derived from beta=1.11, Rf=4.35%, ERP=5.50%
- Terminal growth of 2.10%

Write a one-page summary memo explaining the key assumptions and valuation conclusion. Be specific with numbers. Do NOT use AI hedging.
